_README: Profiles for the eighteen SIMULATED nodes (03-20) of the 20-node hybrid CPS
network -- 10 MPU6050-type + 10 SW-420-type total (2 real + 18 simulated),
grown from the original 10-node/8-simulated network to equalise sensor-type
representation once esp32-vib-002 (SW-420) had real captured data to
calibrate against (see sw420_measured below). esp32-sim-03..10 are the
original profiles; esp32-sim-11..20 are the addition.
JSON, not YAML, deliberately: docs/11 records dropping pyyaml from
this project's dependency list, and pyyaml is not installed. Adding a
dependency to hold eight dictionaries would be exactly the kind of
convenience the project already decided against.
WHAT THESE ARE. Each profile perturbs statistics MEASURED from the real
hardware, in documented directions, with its own frozen seed. They are not
duplicates of real telemetry, and they are not real telemetry with noise
added on top -- each is an independent draw from a generator whose
parameters are offsets from the measured real ones.
WHAT THEY ARE NOT. They are not physical devices, they are never described
as such, and every record they produce carries source_type = SIMULATED.
Their role is controlled network-scale relational context for the
coordinated/distributed anomaly experiments -- not physical evidence.
MEASURED REFERENCE (TRAIN-split real at-rest rows only, n=103, from
sessions 20260902_171313 and 20260902_102448; the VALIDATION and TEST
sessions are NOT consulted, or the simulator would be parameterised from
data it is later evaluated against):
crest_factor   mean 0.0190  sd 0.0130
kurtosis       mean -0.0588 sd 1.0812
dominant_freq  mean 82.22   sd 58.75    (nominal-rate bin index, not Hz)
rms lag-1 autocorrelation 0.5874
Deliberately NOT done: no profile was given an extreme parameter to make
the GNN look better. The variation spans a plausible range around the
measured device and stops there. Nodes 08 and 09 are HARDER than the real
node, not easier.

at_rest.note: trigger_rate, duty_cycle, burst_max_ms and inter_event_cv are all EXACTLY 0.0 across every one of the 140 at-rest rows -- the real board produced zero false triggers at rest. No spread exists to measure from this sample; rest_* baseline parameters below are anchored at this true zero rather than a datasheet guess, and rest_cv/noise sd terms stay a documented judgement call, not a measurement, for the same reason ADR-18 gives for MPU6050 spread: one session cannot establish a distribution from a constant.

sw420_note: esp32-sim-07/10's rest_* parameters were originally the SENSOR's
documented behaviour (contact closure duration, comparator threshold),
not a measurement, because no SW-420 capture existed yet. Session
20260905_162002 now exists (TRAIN split only -- no held-out SW-420
session, see data/splits/session_split.json) and both profiles plus the
esp32-sim-11..20 SW-420-type additions below are anchored to it: rest
state at true zero, anomaly magnitude_scale chosen so the simulated
disturbance response spans the measured gentle_tap..tilt_rotate range

nodes.variation: Quiet, well-mounted machine. Baseline slightly below the real device, tightest spread of the eight.
Higher DC baseline (different mounting angle changes the gravity projection) and moderately noisier.
Loose mount: much noisier, heavy timing jitter, fatter kurtosis tail. The noisiest normal node.
Slow thermal drift: baseline wanders across the session rather than staying stationary. Tests whether the normal region tolerates drift.

SW-420-like. Sensitive threshold: fires occasionally even at rest, so its resting duty cycle is non-zero -- the measured real board (session 20260905_162002) was completely silent at rest (0/140), so this is now a deliberately WORSE-than-measured node representing a looser/more sensitive mount, not the typical case.
HARD CASE. Anomalies at 35% of the real node's magnitude -- close to the noise floor. Included precisely because it lowers the reported detection rate.
Slow-developing fault: anomalies are long and recover slowly, more like bearing wear than an impact. Sequence-shaped, so it is the case the LSTM-AE should be best at.

SW-420-like. Conservative threshold: silent at rest, fires only on real disturbance. The opposite configuration to node 07, and now the one that MATCHES the measured real board's rest state (0/140 triggers) most closely.
Extra accelerometer on the real bench (group A), vibration-damped mount -- lower baseline noise than sim-03/04. Added to bring the MPU6050-type node count to 10, matching the SW-420-type count.

Second switch node on the real bench (group A). Rest state anchored at the measured real board's true zero (0/140 triggers); disturbance magnitude tuned to the measured gentle_tap mean (trigger_rate ~11/s).

Third switch, group A. Looser bracket than sim-12 -- occasional spurious rest trigger (a documented judgement call, not measured -- see sw420_note); disturbance magnitude tuned near the measured moderate_shake mean (~21/s).
Third accelerometer on machine 2 (group B), off-axis mount -- moderate baseline shift and stronger anomaly transients than sim-05/06.
Machine-2 switch (group B). Silent at rest like the measured board; disturbance magnitude tuned to the measured tilt_rotate mean, the strongest of the four real disturbance phases (~45/s).

Machine-2 switch (group B). Silent at rest; short, intense burst response (impact-prone mount) rather than sustained shaking -- tuned near the measured sharp_impact mean (~38/s), with a short burst/duration rather than sim-15's sustained one.
Machine-2 switch (group B), the SW-420 HARD CASE -- weak/borderline disturbance response near the noise floor, mirroring sim-08's MPU6050 hard-case philosophy for the switch modality.
Fourth accelerometer on machine 3 (group C), a different frequency band than sim-08/09 (secondary shaft speed) -- moderate hard case.
Machine-3 switch (group C). Silent at rest; disturbance magnitude blended between the measured gentle_tap and moderate_shake means.
Machine-3 switch (group C), slow-developing-fault analogue to sim-09's MPU6050 case for the switch modality -- long, growing bursts rather than a brief spike, and slow to recover.
